links.outcome: Concerning chatbot behavior across 13 clinical risk dimensions in multi-turn simulated mental-health conversations
links.effect: Concerning behavior was widespread across 9 target chatbots and 30 simulated user profiles in 810 conversations, though reduced in newer models; it accumulated over turns and was highest when supportive behaviors reinforced user vulnerability.
links.quote: Across 810 conversations, spanning 9 target chatbots and 30 simulated user profiles, concerning behavior in target chatbots was widespread, albeit reduced in newer models.

unlisted_practices: Simulated-user (persona-based) multi-turn auditing of chatbots across clinically grounded risk dimensions
Intervening at early escalation points in conversations to reduce cumulative risk

screen.reason: The study develops and applies a clinical red-teaming/auditing framework (SIM-VAIL) using simulated vulnerable patient profiles to test safety risks across commercial LLMs and examines early escalation intervention guardrails.

primary.practice: simulated user red-teaming safety audit framework and early conversational escalation interventions
